picks.excerpt: Nvidia ACE, the tech behind PUBG's generative-AI team mates, is coming to creature-collecting RPG Aniimo in early 2027, letting players talk to creatures driven by a locally-run Nemotron small language model.
picks.rationale: Conversational NPCs stop being a demo: a shipping RPG runs a local small language model, so character and dialogue designers now have a real production target.

picks.excerpt: NVIDIA brings the next wave of RTX gaming to Gamescom, with publishers adopting new AI-accelerated visual quality and anti-cheat technology on RTX Spark hardware.
picks.rationale: First-party account of which AI rendering and anti-cheat features publishers are actually adopting — the baseline art and performance targets for the next round of PC titles.

picks.excerpt: Five Nordic industry voices explain how AI is reshaping studio culture, creative roles, team structure and legal risk — a ground-level look at AI-native production practice.
picks.rationale: Concrete studio-level practice rather than opinion: how teams restructure roles and manage legal exposure when AI enters the pipeline.

picks.excerpt: Final Fantasy: Crystal Chronicles composer Kumi Tanioka says an AI-generated album was published under her name on Spotify, exposing how weak identity controls are for game creators' catalogues.
picks.rationale: A named game creator's identity was hijacked on a major platform — a direct warning about how little protects a credited artist's catalogue right now.

picks.excerpt: Humankind 2's reveal trailer was immediately accused of using generative AI for its live-action shots; the developer confirmed no AI was used, showing how AI suspicion now shapes reveal-art craft.
picks.rationale: Human-made key art is now guilty until proven innocent — reveal trailers need provenance and craft choices planned as part of the marketing brief.
